description: Create AI model photos and videos for fashion brands: on-body shots, lookbook scenes, and outfit reels from flat lay or hanger photos. Try it on your next drop.
h1: AI Model Photos and Videos for Fashion Brands and Boutiques
lead: AI model photos and videos for fashion brands turn a flat lay or hanger photo into images of the piece being worn, styled lookbook scenes, and short outfit clips for Reels and TikTok.
card: Flat lay to on-model photos, lookbook scenes and short outfit clips.
intro: Clothing sells on fit and movement. Someone looking at a linen dress wants to know where the hem lands, how the fabric drapes, and what to pair it with. Flat lays and hanger shots show the cut and the print, but they rarely answer those questions, and booking a model for every new arrival adds up fast for a small label.

Upload a clean photo of the garment and describe how it should be worn: walking down a city street, seated on a stool in a bright studio, or styled as a full look for a lookbook page. For motion, a short vertical clip of someone turning in the outfit shows swing and drape in a way a still can't. Let your size chart and measurements do the job of explaining fit.

ideas.d: Show each new arrival being worn against a plain backdrop, so it sits neatly beside your other product photos and shoppers can judge length and silhouette.
Style a trench coat on a rainy street or a sundress on a boardwalk for a collection page, a newsletter, or Instagram posts announcing the drop.
A 6- to 15-second vertical clip of the outfit turning, walking, or sitting shows movement. Add music and captions afterward in TikTok or CapCut.
Ask for a styled image with open space to one side, then type your discount and end date over it in Canva or Ads Manager so the numbers are exactly right.

faq.q: Can I turn a flat lay photo into an on-model photo?
faq.a: Yes. Lay the garment flat or hang it on a plain wall, smooth out the wrinkles, and photograph the whole piece in even light. Then describe the person and setting, for example "full-length, standing in a bright studio."

faq.q: Will the AI change my print or fabric?
faq.a: It works from your photo, so fine stripes, embroidery, and buttons hold up when the upload is sharp and close. Look carefully at patterns and trims before you list the image, and make another version if anything has drifted.

faq.q: Can I show my clothes on a plus-size or petite model?
faq.a: You can describe the person you want to see, including height, build, and age range, such as "petite woman in her 40s" or "tall man with a broad frame." Showing your real customer helps shoppers picture themselves in the piece.

faq.q: How do I make a TikTok video of my clothes being worn?
faq.a: Choose 9:16 and a length of 6, 10, or 15 seconds, then describe the movement, like a slow turn or a walk toward the camera. Videos are made one at a time, so run another if you want the same outfit in a different setting.
